summary: The NDO Fairness Act of 2025 modifies the requirements and procedures for the government to obtain nondisclosure orders (NDOs) under the Stored Communications Act. These orders temporarily stop communication and remote computing service providers from telling customers or subscribers that the government has sought their records or electronic communications. The bill raises the legal standards required to get an NDO, limits the duration of NDOs, introduces mandatory court reviews, requires notice to targets when NDOs expire, and mandates annual reporting by the Department of Justice.

affected_groups.effect: Must meet higher evidentiary standards, secure written court determinations, adhere to stricter time limits, provide post-expiration notices to targets, and compile detailed annual reports regarding NDO usage.
Subject to explicit NDO timeframes and narrow tailoring rules, and given specific legal pathways to challenge unreasonable or unlawful nondisclosure orders in court.
affected_groups.group: Electronic Communication and Remote Computing Service Providers

affected_groups.effect: Guaranteed eventual notification when their records have been requested or obtained by the government via an expired NDO, along with the right to request copies of the disclosed information.
Specific metrics regarding NDOs targeting news media members and First Amendment-protected activities must be tracked and reported annually by the Department of Justice.

key_provisions: Raises the standard for obtaining an NDO, requiring a court to issue a written determination based on specific and articulable facts showing that failing to grant the order would result in negative outcomes like endangering safety, flight from prosecution, destruction of evidence, witness intimidation, or seriously jeopardizing an investigation.
Limits the duration of initial NDOs to a maximum of 90 days for most investigations, but allows up to one year for investigations regarding child pornography or sexual exploitation of children.
Allows the government to request 90-day extensions, which require a new written court determination.
Grants communication and remote computing service providers the legal opportunity to challenge and ask the court to modify or vacate unreasonable or unlawful NDOs.
Requires the government to notify the named customer or subscriber within 5 business days after an NDO expires, providing a copy of the warrant or subpoena and information regarding the inquiry.

Requires the Attorney General to submit and publish an annual report detailing statistics on NDO applications, orders, denials, impacts on news media members, and resulting arrests, trials, and convictions.
missing_information: The exact financial cost or budgetary appropriations required to implement the new reporting and legal procedures.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The NDO Fairness Act of 2025 modifies the requirements and procedures for the government to obtain nondisclosure orders (NDOs) under the Stored Communications Act. These orders temporarily stop communication and remote computing service providers from telling customers or subscribers that the government has sought their records or electronic communications. The bill raises the legal standards required to get an NDO, limits the duration of NDOs, introduces mandatory court reviews, requires notice to targets when NDOs expire, and mandates annual reporting by the Department of Justice.
summary_detail.significance: This bill alters the balance between government investigative secrecy and customer notification rights regarding electronic communications records, establishing strict judicial oversight, standardized time caps, and transparency measures.
